items.content:
How to Get the Most Out of Oh-My-Hermes

Simply put, Oh-My-Hermes (OMH) is an intelligence pack that makes Hermes Agent insanely good just by plugging it in.

Today, instead of just a basic intro, here’s a quick guide on how to actually use it and the impact it brings.

1. Set up subagent routing 
Whether you use omh-model, omh-model-setup, or just ask the agent, OMH routes each task category to the right model (e.g., ultrabrain, visual-engineering, deep-work).
Recommended setups are in the README. Just configure the categories for your setup, and the right model will run automatically when handling subagent tasks.

2. Memory system 
OMH comes with long-term memory—turn it on, and retention goes way up.
It mixes in smart mechanics like filesystem labeling, semantic search, TTL, and more.
If you want to audit or organize what the agent remembers, try using the `memory-sync` skill. It presents stored, ambiguous, or cluttered memories so you can clean them up easily.

3. Calling tons of skills isn't recommended, but definitely know `ulw-XYZ` 
The Ultra-Work skills prefixed with `ulw-` handle loops, goal engineering via plan skills, coding rules, and parallel tasks to push execution through the most optimized path.
Other skills can be called manually or auto-routed (ulw has auto-routing too), but just dropping a quick "ulw-work let's go" into your prompt works even better.

4. The TUI looks slick
The TUI is becoming standalone. OMH’s TUI provides live viewers for parallel subagent routing, omh todo, and more. It looks great, so definitely give it a try.

Install Oh-My-Hermes:
https://t.co/g1exHwWcg6

#hermes

items.title: @HermesWatcher @witcheer @NousResearch That's how it was before, and the amount of issues we had to ...
items.content:
@HermesWatcher @witcheer @NousResearch That's how it was before, and the amount of issues we had to deal with because people's DBs grew bigger than their resources could handle, where they wouldnt be able to create or continue sessions because disk was full, etc became intense.

Our goal is a default happier path, that causes less users issues. If you have an alternative to either I'd be open to it, maybe something that detects size of db, disk space, and asks if you want to prune/warns that you should prune when it detects unsafe?

He defends the new default path and invites alternatives, suggesting an approach that detects DB size and disk space and warns or prompts users to prune.
items.reasoning: Substantive design rationale straight from the lead developer, addressing a likely community complaint and openly soliciting feedback on a pruning/warning mechanism. Decent engagement (31 likes, 9 replies) and insight into product direction.
